description: Scored US public sector briefs from official government data: product safety recalls (CPSC, NHTSA, FDA food), political money (FEC, Senate lobbying), federal spending (USAspending, Treasury), natural hazards (FEMA, USGS, NWS), cyber threat (CISA KEV, NVD), respiratory illness (CDC), wildfire activity (NIFC), climate anomaly (NOAA), crime (FBI), air travel demand (TSA), federal rulemaking (Federal Register) and Medicare enrollment (CMS). Each brief is a 0-100 score with label, trend versus the horizon, the inputs that drive it, risk flags, confidence and a citation for every input. POST /v1/brief {vertical} returns one scored brief; POST /v1/overview returns every brief at once; POST /v1/verticals lists them. Verticals: product-recalls (Are consumer product, vehicle or food recalls rising?); political-money (Is outside election spending or lobbying activity rising?); federal-spending (Is federal spending accelerating, and in which agencies?); natural-hazards (Are disasters, severe weather and earthquakes running above normal?); cyber-threat (Are actively exploited software flaws rising?); disease-activity (Is respiratory illness (COVID-19, flu, RSV) rising in the US?); wildfire-activity (Is the US wildfire season running above normal?); climate-anomaly (How far are US temperature and precipitation from normal?); public-safety (Is US crime rising or falling?); travel-demand (Are more people flying than a year ago?); rulemaking (Is the federal government issuing more regulations than usual?); medicare-providers (Is Medicare enrollment growing, and is it shifting to Medicare Advantage?). Raw scored series: /v1/signals, /v1/signal, /v1/explain, /v1/catalog. Every response is a single JSON object. Research signal, not investment advice.

rpc_types.notes: POST /v1/verticals, POST /v1/brief, POST /v1/overview, POST /v1/signals, POST /v1/signal, POST /v1/explain, POST /v1/catalog; GET /v1/version, /v1/health. JSON body only. Bad input returns 400 + JSON.

serving.backend: Node.js HTTP server (zero npm dependencies) behind a RelayMiner at http://<container>:8080. No caller auth. Answers come from a private hub refreshed by a scheduled collector of official public data; 5-minute cache.
serving.notes: Gateway operators: configure as type passthrough with rpc_types ["rest"].
